children: Moleculin Biotech announced preclinical data showing Annamycin’s antitumor activity in pancreatic cancer is partially mediated by CD8+ T cells.
Annamycin showed antitumor activity in pancreatic cancer models partly dependent on CD8+ T cell cytotoxicity.
Findings suggest Annamycin may convert immunologically “cold” tumors to “hot,” enabling immune attack.
Data were presented at the AACR Conference on Pancreatic Cancer (Sept 25–28, 2026) in San Diego.
Results are preclinical; Annamycin is not currently in clinical development for pancreatic cancer.
Company notes potential for combination strategies and complements its WP1066 immune-modulating program.

title: Moleculin Biotech: Preclinical Data Suggest Annamycin’s Pancreatic Activity Involves CD8+ T Cells
